This is a large task. 

Relevant reference proof functions have been sorted out, the task requirements have been clarified, and it has been confirmed that the sealed baseline can complete batch verification and fork identification of fork aggregate alternative chains, but lacks signing and cross-site adjudication capabilities.

The new chain fork proof signing feature reuses existing batch chain items and two shared policies. It first runs existing batch verification to generate offline proof only when forks are detected, and binds relevant chain information, policy details and identity information in the proof payload.

The new chain fork proof verification feature only requires proof, two policies, a keyring and timestamp to complete offline recheck. It will independently recalculate relevant chain parameters, reject any binding mismatch, and verify the validity of signature credentials. The new batch proof verification interface will first check the proof list, keep the order of batch reports, non-item failures will not block subsequent items, and the failure result will be empty.

The statuses returned by the new batch proof verification interface follow the priority order of verified, invalid-proof and unauthenticated, with a dedicated independent copy for success results. The new chain fork adjudication feature generates standard signed adjudication packages based on proof lists and site threshold policies, and each proof will be rechecked first before being authorized precisely.

Clarification has been made on three types of fork judgment results: duplicate, conflict and insufficient. A new interface is added for offline verification of chain fork decisions.

Error classification for all public interfaces has been finalized: specified exceptions are triggered for different invalid scenarios, no file operations are performed or input values are modified, and public commands and existing interfaces remain unchanged in the README.

All relevant functions map to the existing prune aggregate fork proof and adjudication family, and I will read the template functions to clarify the implementation details.

24696	def _tally_pac_fork_rows(
24697	    rows: list[dict],
24698	) -> tuple[bool, dict[str, _PAFD_EDGE_SET]]:
24699	    """Group authenticated rows per site by their complete edge sets.
24700	
24701	    Two rows from one site are the same declaration only when their
24702	    complete fork edge set -- every ``(rootDigest, predecessorDigest,
24703	    successors)`` triple -- agrees, regardless of the proof digest.
24704	    The smallest-id row of one identical set is the vote and extras are
24705	    ``duplicate``, while two distinct edge sets from one site are both a
24706	    ``contradiction``.  Returns ``(contradicted, votes)`` where
24707	    ``votes`` maps each non-contradicting site to its one edge set.
24708	    """
24709	    by_site: dict[str, dict[_PAFD_EDGE_SET, list[dict]]] = {}
24710	    for row in rows:
24711	        if row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] in (
24712	            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID,
24713	            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE,
24714	            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION,
24715	        ):
24716	            by_site.setdefault(row[VD_ISSUER], {}).setdefault(
24717	                _pafd_content(row), []
24718	            ).append(row)
24719	
24720	    contradicted = False
24721	    votes: dict[str, _PAFD_EDGE_SET] = {}
24722	    for site, groups in by_site.items():
24723	        if len(groups) > 1:
24724	            contradicted = True
24725	            ordered_groups = sorted(
24726	                groups.values(),
24727	                key=lambda members: min(member[ID] for member in members),
24728	            )
24729	            for members in ordered_groups:
24730	                members.sort(key=lambda row: row[ID])
24731	                members[0][ADJ_CONCLUSION] = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION
24732	                members[0][ADJ_REASON] = REASON_CONTRADICTION
24733	                for extra in members[1:]:
24734	                    extra[ADJ_CONCLUSION] = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE
24735	                    extra[ADJ_REASON] = REASON_DUPLICATE
24736	        else:
24737	            content, members = next(iter(groups.items()))
24738	            members.sort(key=lambda row: row[ID])
24739	            members[0][ADJ_CONCLUSION] = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID
24740	            members[0][ADJ_REASON] = None
24741	            for extra in members[1:]:
24742	                extra[ADJ_CONCLUSION] = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE
24743	                extra[ADJ_REASON] = REASON_DUPLICATE
24744	            votes[site] = content

24767	    fork proof rules, then authorized by the exact signing site and key

24770	    unauthorized proof rejects just that item with one fixed reason

24772	    ``credential-unavailable``, ``revoked``, ``not-yet-valid``,

24779	    predecessor digest and the sorted legal successor digests; any

25131	def _reconcile_pafd(payload: dict, threshold: int) -> str:
25132	    """Re-derive every aggregate binding of a parsed fork decision.
25133	
25134	    Re-tallies the per-proof rows the signature covers -- row ordering,
25135	    proof digests, duplicate/contradiction conclusions, the cross-site
25136	    complete-edge-set agreement, the threshold acceptance and the
25137	    claimed common set -- without seeing any fork proof.  Any mismatch
25138	    raises :class:`InvalidAggregateForkDecisionError`; otherwise the
25139	    derived status is returned.
25140	    """
25141	    rows = payload[ITEMS]
25142	    proofs = payload[PAFD_PROOFS]
25143	    if len(rows) != len(proofs):
25144	        raise _pafd_invalid(
25145	            "the items must cover every proof and vice versa"
25146	        )
25147	    expected_order = sorted(
25148	        rows,
25149	        key=lambda row: (
25150	            row[VD_ISSUER] is not None,
25151	            row[VD_ISSUER] or "",
25152	            row[ID],
25153	        ),
25154	    )
25155	    if [row[ID] for row in expected_order] != [row[ID] for row in rows]:
25156	        raise _pafd_invalid("items must be sorted by site then id")
25157	    row_digests = [row[PAFD_FORK_PROOF_DIGEST] for row in rows]
25158	    if sorted(row_digests) != sorted(proofs):
25159	        raise _pafd_invalid(
25160	            "the bound proof digests must equal the per-item digests"
25161	        )
25162	
25163	    by_site: dict[str, dict[_PAFD_EDGE_SET, list[dict]]] = {}
25164	    for row in rows:
25165	        if row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] == _PAFD_CONCLUSION_INVALID:
25166	            continue
25167	        by_site.setdefault(row[VD_ISSUER], {}).setdefault(
25168	            _pafd_content(row), []
25169	        ).append(row)
25170	
25171	    contradicted = False
25172	    votes: dict[str, _PAFD_EDGE_SET] = {}
25173	    for site, groups in by_site.items():
25174	        if len(groups) > 1:
25175	            contradicted = True
25176	            expected_conclusion = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION
25177	            expected_reason = REASON_CONTRADICTION
25178	        else:
25179	            expected_conclusion = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID
25180	            expected_reason = None
25181	            votes[site] = next(iter(groups.keys()))
25182	        for members_raw in groups.values():
25183	            members = sorted(members_raw, key=lambda row: row[ID])
25184	            for index, row in enumerate(members):
25185	                if index == 0:
25186	                    if row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] != expected_conclusion:
25187	                        raise _pafd_invalid(
25188	                            f"item {row[ID]!r} has the wrong conclusion"
25189	                        )
25190	                    if row[ADJ_REASON] != expected_reason:
25191	                        raise _pafd_invalid(
25192	                            f"item {row[ID]!r} has the wrong reason"
25193	                        )
25194	                else:
25195	                    if row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] != _PAFD_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE:
25196	                        raise _pafd_invalid(
25197	                            f"item {row[ID]!r} must be a duplicate"
25198	                        )
25199	                    if row[ADJ_REASON] != REASON_DUPLICATE:
25200	                        raise _pafd_invalid(
25201	                            f"item {row[ID]!r} must carry the duplicate "
25202	                            "reason"
25203	                        )
25204	            representative = members[0]
25205	            for row in members[1:]:
25206	                if _pac_fork_edge_triples(
25207	                    row[PAFD_EDGES]
25208	                ) != _pac_fork_edge_triples(representative[PAFD_EDGES]):
25209	                    raise _pafd_invalid(
25210	                        f"item {row[ID]!r} duplicates a proof with a "
25211	                        "different fork edge set"
25212	                    )
25213	
25214	    edge_sets = set(votes.values())
25215	    if contradicted or len(edge_sets) > 1:
25216	        status = _PAFD_STATUS_CONFLICTED
25217	        expected_common = None
25218	    elif len(edge_sets) == 1 and len(votes) >= threshold:
25219	        status = _PAFD_STATUS_ACCEPTED
25220	        expected_common = _sorted_pac_fork_edge_objects(
25221	            next(iter(edge_sets))
25222	        )
25223	    elif len(edge_sets) == 1:

25228	    else:

25241	def verify_prune_aggregate_fork_decision(
25242	    decision, prune_policy, site_policy, keyring, moment
25243	):
25244	    """Re-verify a signed prune aggregate fork decision entirely offline.
25245	
25246	    Only the decision bytes, the expected shared ``prune_policy``, the
25247	    expected ``site_policy``, the current ``keyring`` and the
25248	    verification ``moment`` are consulted -- no file is read or written
25249	    and no argument is modified.  Verification validates the canonical
25250	    encoding and every key set, recomputes both policy digests, re-tallies
25251	    the bound per-proof rows purely from the signed payload (the
25252	    original-order proof digest bindings, the site/id row ordering, the
25253	    same-site duplicate/contradiction markings, the cross-site complete
25254	    fork-edge-set agreement, the threshold outcome and the claimed
25255	    common set), and checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the *current*
25256	    keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version, usable at
25257	    the verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry rejects
25258	    the decision with no fallback.
25259	
25260	    On success a fresh mapping is returned with the fixed keys
25261	    ``common``, ``decisionDigest`` (the SHA-256 of the decision bytes),
25262	    ``issuer``, ``items``, ``keyVersion``, ``prunePolicyDigest``,
25263	    ``proofs``, ``sitePolicyDigest``, ``status`` and ``version`` (the
25264	    integer 1).  A non-bytes decision or a public field of the wrong
25265	    type raises :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an
25266	    int); an illegal prune/site policy, keyring or moment raises
25267	    :class:`ValueError`; an illegal encoding, key set, digest, ordering,
25268	    tally or binding raises
25269	    :class:`InvalidAggregateForkDecisionError` (a :class:`ValueError`
25270	    subclass); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials
25271	    or a signature mismatch raise :class:`AuthenticationError`.
25272	    """
25273	    if not isinstance(decision, bytes):
25274	        raise TypeError("decision must be bytes")
25275	    validated_prune_policy = _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
25276	    validated_site_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(site_policy)
25277	    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
25278	    verify_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")
25279	    return _verify_pafd_core(
25280	        decision, validated_prune_policy, validated_site_policy,
25281	        validated_keyring, verify_moment,
25282	    )

25285	def _verify_pafd_core(

25287	    validated_prune_policy: dict,
25288	    validated_site_policy: dict,
25289	    validated_keyring: dict[str, list[dict]],

25291	) -> dict:
25292	    """Verify one fork decision against already-validated shared materials.
25293	
25294	    This is the shared core of
25295	    :func:`verify_prune_aggregate_fork_decision` and the batch
25296	    :func:`verify_prune_aggregate_fork_decisions`; the caller owns the
25297	    argument-type and shared-material validation.  The returned dict is
25298	    freshly built solely from authenticated decision material.
25299	    """
25300	    payload, signature = _parse_pafd(decision)
25301	    expected_prune_digest = hashlib.sha256(

25319	    )

25332	        for key, value in (
25333	            (PAFD_COMMON, payload[PAFD_COMMON]),

def _pac_fork_proofs_item_report(
    item_id: str, status: str, error: str | None, result: dict | None
) -> dict:
    """One fork-proof batch report with the fixed key order."""
    return {
        CHECKPOINT_ITEM_ERROR: error,
        ID: item_id,
        VERDICT_ITEM_RESULT: result,
        STATUS: status,
    }


def _verify_pac_fork_proof_item(
    item: dict,
    validated_prune_policy: dict,
    validated_keyring: dict[str, list[dict]],
    moment: int,
) -> dict:
    """Verify one prune aggregate fork proof in isolation.

    Unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials and a wrong
    signature make the item ``unauthenticated``; every encoding,
    key-set, version, digest, ordering, reference or report-binding
    fault makes it ``invalid-proof``; a passing proof is ``verified``.
    """
    item_id = item[ID]
    proof = item[FORK_PROOF_ITEM_PROOF]
    try:
        result = _verify_pac_fork_proof_core(
            proof, validated_prune_policy, validated_keyring, moment
        )
    except AuthenticationError as exc:
        return _pac_fork_proofs_item_report(
            item_id, _PAC_FORK_PROOFS_UNAUTHENTICATED, str(exc), None
        )
    except (InvalidAggregateForkProofError, TypeError) as exc:
        # A TypeError here can only come from a wrong JSON field type
        # *inside* the proof bytes; the public argument types were all
        # validated before the batch ran.
        return _pac_fork_proofs_item_report(
            item_id, _PAC_FORK_PROOFS_INVALID, str(exc), None
        )
    return _pac_fork_proofs_item_report(
        item_id, _PAC_FORK_PROOFS_VERIFIED, None, result
    )


def verify_prune_aggregate_fork_proofs(
    items: list, prune_policy: dict, keyring: dict, moment: int
) -> dict:
    """Verify a whole batch of prune aggregate fork proofs offline.

    ``items`` is a non-empty list; each item is a dict with exactly the
    keys ``id`` (a non-empty str, unique across the batch) and ``proof``
    (the bytes :func:`sign_prune_aggregate_fork_proof` produced).
    ``prune_policy`` is the shared invariant original pruning policy and
    ``keyring``/``moment`` keep their single-proof meaning.  The whole
    batch structure and the shared materials are validated in full
    before any proof is verified: container, element or field type
    faults raise :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an
    int) and an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key
    set raises :class:`ValueError` (policy, keyring and moment keep
    their single-entry classification).  Only these batch-level faults
    raise.

    Each proof is then verified independently, in strict input order,
    through the exact :func:`verify_prune_aggregate_fork_proof` rules:
    one proof's failure never stops a later proof or alters an earlier
    report.  Unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a
    wrong signature make the item ``unauthenticated``; an illegal
    encoding, key set, version, digest, count, ordering, reference or
    report binding makes it ``invalid-proof``; a passing proof is
    ``verified``.

    The top-level result is a fresh dict with the fixed keys ``items``
    and ``version`` (the integer 1); each item report carries, in this
    key order, ``error`` (null exactly when verified), ``id``,
    ``result`` (a fresh independent copy of the single-entry result
    when verified, otherwise null) and ``status``.  Repeated calls
    return equal but mutually independent results.  No file is read or
    written and no input is modified.
    """
    validated_items = _validated_pac_fork_proof_items(items)
    validated_prune_policy = _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
    verify_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")
    return {
        ITEMS: [
            _verify_pac_fork_proof_item(
                item, validated_prune_policy, validated_keyring, verify_moment
            )
            for item in validated_items
        ],
        VERSION: PAC_FORK_PROOFS_VERSION,
    }

# -- Multi-site threshold adjudication over prune aggregate fork proofs --------

class InvalidAggregateForkDecisionError(ValueError):
    """A signed prune aggregate fork decision breaks its binding contract."""


def _pafd_invalid(message: str) -> InvalidAggregateForkDecisionError:
    return InvalidAggregateForkDecisionError(
        f"invalid prune aggregate fork decision: {message}"
    )


def _reject_duplicate_pafd_keys(pairs: list[tuple]) -> dict:
    """``object_pairs_hook`` turning duplicate decision keys into an error."""
    result: dict = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise _pafd_invalid(f"duplicate key {key!r} in object")
        result[key] = value
    return result


def _pac_fork_edge_object(entry: dict) -> dict:
    """One canonical ``{rootDigest, predecessorDigest, successors}`` edge."""
    return {
        PAC_ROOT_DIGEST: entry[PAC_ROOT_DIGEST],
        PAC_PREDECESSOR_DIGEST: entry[PAC_PREDECESSOR_DIGEST],
        PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS: list(entry[PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS]),
    }


def _pac_fork_proof_edges(payload: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """The complete fork edge set a verified fork proof binds.

    The proof parser already validated every fork entry, its ordering
    and its successor set, so the entries are copied verbatim in the
    report's own canonical (root, predecessor, successor) order.
    """
    return [
        _pac_fork_edge_object(fork)
        for fork in payload[FORK_PROOF_REPORT][CHAINS_FORKS]
    ]


def _pac_fork_edge_triples(
    edges: list[dict],
) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, tuple[str, ...]], ...]:
    """Order-preserving edge objects to comparable triples."""
    return tuple(
        (
            edge[PAC_ROOT_DIGEST],
            edge[PAC_PREDECESSOR_DIGEST],
            tuple(edge[PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS]),
        )
        for edge in edges
    )


def _sorted_pac_fork_edge_objects(
    triples: set | frozenset,
) -> list[dict]:
    """Unique fork edges sorted by (rootDigest, predecessorDigest, ...)."""
    return [
        {
            PAC_ROOT_DIGEST: root_digest,
            PAC_PREDECESSOR_DIGEST: predecessor,
            PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS: list(successors),
        }
        for root_digest, predecessor, successors in sorted(triples)
    ]


def _validated_pafd_edge(value: object, where: str) -> dict:
    """Validate one bound fork edge object into a fresh ordered dict."""
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise TypeError(f"{where} edge must be an object")
    if set(value.keys()) != _PAFD_EDGE_KEYS:
        raise _pafd_invalid(
            f"{where} edge must contain exactly the keys 'predecessorDigest', "
            "'rootDigest' and 'successors'"
        )
    root_digest = value[PAC_ROOT_DIGEST]
    predecessor = value[PAC_PREDECESSOR_DIGEST]
    successors = value[PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS]
    if not isinstance(root_digest, str):
        raise TypeError(f"{where} edge rootDigest must be a str")
    if not isinstance(predecessor, str):
        raise TypeError(f"{where} edge predecessorDigest must be a str")
    if not _prune_is_digest(root_digest):
        raise _pafd_invalid(
            f"{where} edge rootDigest must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
        )
    if not _prune_is_digest(predecessor):
        raise _pafd_invalid(
            f"{where} edge predecessorDigest must be 64 lowercase hex "
            "characters"
        )
    if not isinstance(successors, list):
        raise TypeError(f"{where} edge successors must be a list")
    if not successors:
        raise _pafd_invalid(f"{where} edge successors must be non-empty")
    for position, successor in enumerate(successors):
        if not isinstance(successor, str):
            raise TypeError(
                f"{where} edge successor {position} must be a str"
            )
        if not _prune_is_digest(successor):
            raise _pafd_invalid(
                f"{where} edge successor {position} must be 64 lowercase "
                "hex characters"
            )
    if successors != sorted(successors) or len(set(successors)) != len(
        successors
    ):
        raise _pafd_invalid(
            f"{where} edge successors must be unique and sorted ascending"
        )
    return {
        PAC_ROOT_DIGEST: root_digest,
        PAC_PREDECESSOR_DIGEST: predecessor,
        PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS: list(successors),
    }


def _pafd_row(
    item_id: str,
    proof_digest: str,
    site: str | None,
    key_version: int | None,
    edges: list[dict] | None,
    conclusion: str,
    reason: str | None,
) -> dict:
    """One per-proof decision row with the fixed bound key set."""
    return {
        ADJ_CONCLUSION: conclusion,
        PAFD_EDGES: edges,
        ID: item_id,
        KEY_VERSION: key_version,
        PAFD_FORK_PROOF_DIGEST: proof_digest,
        ADJ_REASON: reason,
        VD_ISSUER: site,
    }


def _adjudicate_pac_fork_one(
    item: dict,
    prune_policy_digest: str,
    site_policy: dict,
    keyring: dict[str, list[dict]],
    moment: int,
) -> dict:
    """Verify, authorize and authenticate one fork proof in isolation.

    The proof is first checked through the exact
    :func:`verify_prune_aggregate_fork_proof` structural rules, then the
    signing site and key version are authorized exactly against the site
    policy with no fallback, and finally the HMAC is checked against the
    current keyring.  Any failure rejects just this row with one fixed
    reason and never affects the other items.
    """
    item_id = item[ID]
    raw_proof = item[FORK_PROOF_ITEM_PROOF]
    proof_digest = hashlib.sha256(raw_proof).hexdigest()

    def structural_invalid() -> dict:
        return _pafd_row(
            item_id, proof_digest, None, None, None,
            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_INVALID, _PAFD_REASON_INVALID_PROOF,
        )

    try:
        payload, signature, _chains = _parse_pac_fork_proof(raw_proof)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return structural_invalid()

    site = payload[VD_ISSUER]
    key_version = payload[KEY_VERSION]
    try:
        edges = _pac_fork_proof_edges(payload)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return structural_invalid()

    def reject(reason: str) -> dict:
        return _pafd_row(
            item_id, proof_digest, site, key_version, edges,
            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_INVALID, reason,
        )

    # The proof must be bound to the exact shared prune policy and must
    # not be dated after the adjudication moment; a mismatch makes the
    # claimed identity untrustworthy, so the row carries none.
    if payload[RECEIPT_POLICY] != prune_policy_digest:
        return structural_invalid()
    if payload[CP_MOMENT] > moment:
        return structural_invalid()

    allowed_versions = site_policy[ADJ_SITES].get(site)
    if allowed_versions is None:
        return reject(REASON_UNAUTHORIZED_SITE)
    if key_version not in allowed_versions:
        return reject(REASON_UNAUTHORIZED_VERSION)

    key_entry = None
    for candidate in keyring.get(site, ()):
        if candidate[VERSION] == key_version:
            key_entry = candidate
            break
    if key_entry is None:
        return reject(REASON_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE)
    if key_entry[REVOKED]:
        return reject(REASON_REVOKED)
    if moment < key_entry[NOT_BEFORE]:
        return reject(REASON_NOT_YET_VALID)
    if moment > key_entry[NOT_AFTER]:
        return reject(REASON_EXPIRED)

    expected_signature = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(key_entry[SECRET]),
        _prune_compact(payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected_signature, signature):
        return reject(REASON_BAD_SIGNATURE)

    return _pafd_row(
        item_id, proof_digest, site, key_version, edges,
        _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID, None,
    )


_PAFD_EDGE_SET = frozenset[tuple[str, str, tuple[str, ...]]]


def _pafd_content(row: dict) -> _PAFD_EDGE_SET:
    """The complete fork edge set one authenticated row declares."""
    return frozenset(_pac_fork_edge_triples(row[PAFD_EDGES]))


def _tally_pac_fork_rows(
    rows: list[dict],
) -> tuple[bool, dict[str, _PAFD_EDGE_SET]]:
    """Group authenticated rows per site by their complete edge sets.

    Two rows from one site are the same declaration only when their
    complete fork edge set -- every ``(rootDigest, predecessorDigest,
    successors)`` triple -- agrees, regardless of the proof digest.
    The smallest-id row of one identical set is the vote and extras are
    ``duplicate``, while two distinct edge sets from one site are both a
    ``contradiction``.  Returns ``(contradicted, votes)`` where
    ``votes`` maps each non-contradicting site to its one edge set.
    """
    by_site: dict[str, dict[_PAFD_EDGE_SET, list[dict]]] = {}
    for row in rows:
        if row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] in (
            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID,
            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE,
            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION,
        ):
            by_site.setdefault(row[VD_ISSUER], {}).setdefault(
                _pafd_content(row), []
            ).append(row)

    contradicted = False
    votes: dict[str, _PAFD_EDGE_SET] = {}
    for site, groups in by_site.items():
        if len(groups) > 1:
            contradicted = True
            ordered_groups = sorted(
                groups.values(),
                key=lambda members: min(member[ID] for member in members),
            )
            for members in ordered_groups:
                members.sort(key=lambda row: row[ID])
                members[0][ADJ_CONCLUSION] = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION
                members[0][ADJ_REASON] = REASON_CONTRADICTION
                for extra in members[1:]:
                    extra[ADJ_CONCLUSION] = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE
                    extra[ADJ_REASON] = REASON_DUPLICATE
        else:
            content, members = next(iter(groups.items()))
            members.sort(key=lambda row: row[ID])
            members[0][ADJ_CONCLUSION] = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID
            members[0][ADJ_REASON] = None
            for extra in members[1:]:
                extra[ADJ_CONCLUSION] = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE
                extra[ADJ_REASON] = REASON_DUPLICATE
            votes[site] = content
    return contradicted, votes


def adjudicate_prune_aggregate_forks(
    items, prune_policy, site_policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version
):
    """Adjudicate multi-site prune aggregate fork proofs offline.

    ``items`` is a non-empty list; each item contains exactly a unique
    non-empty ``id`` and ``proof`` bytes produced by
    :func:`sign_prune_aggregate_fork_proof`.  ``prune_policy`` is the
    shared invariant original ``{"batch","sites","threshold"}`` pruning
    policy the proofs were issued against; ``site_policy`` carries
    exactly ``sites`` (a non-empty map of each authorized non-empty site
    to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and
    ``threshold`` (a positive integer no greater than the site count).
    ``keyring`` follows the existing rules, ``moment`` is the
    non-negative adjudication moment and ``issuer``/``version`` name the
    adjudicator credentials.  No file is read or written and no input is
    modified.

    Every proof is first verified through the existing prune aggregate
    fork proof rules, then authorized by the exact signing site and key
    version its payload names with no fallback, then authenticated
    against the current keyring.  An invalid, unauthenticated or
    unauthorized proof rejects just that item with one fixed reason
    (``invalid-proof``, ``unauthorized-site``, ``unauthorized-version``,
    ``credential-unavailable``, ``revoked``, ``not-yet-valid``,
    ``expired`` or ``bad-signature``) while the later items are still
    processed.  For one site the complete fork edge set counts once --
    extra proofs declaring an identical edge set are ``duplicate`` --
    while distinct valid edge sets from one site are a
    ``contradiction``.  Distinct sites must agree exactly on the
    complete fork edge set made of the root digest, the forking
    predecessor digest and the sorted legal successor digests; any
    contradiction or cross-site disagreement is ``conflicted`` with a
    null common edge set and no majority can outvote it.  A unique edge
    set backed by at least the threshold of distinct sites is
    ``accepted``; the same unique set short of the threshold stays
    ``insufficient`` but keeps that common set; with no valid vote the
    common set is null.

    The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with
    recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte,
    carrying exactly ``payload`` and ``signature``.  The payload binds
    exactly ``common`` (the sorted common fork edge set, or null),
    ``issuer``, ``items`` (the rows stably sorted by site then id, each
    carrying ``conclusion``, its authenticated ``edges`` or null, ``id``,
    ``keyVersion``, ``proofDigest``, ``reason`` and ``site``),
    ``keyVersion``, ``prunePolicyDigest``, ``proofs`` (each proof digest
    in the original input order), ``sitePolicyDigest``, ``status`` and
    ``version`` (the integer 1).  ``signature`` is the lowercase hex
    HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the exact
    issuer/version key.

    A parameter, container or public-field type fault raises
    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int); an empty
    list, an empty or duplicate id, or an illegal prune/site policy,
    threshold, moment, issuer or version raises :class:`ValueError`;
    unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired adjudicator credentials
    raise :class:`AuthenticationError`.
    """
    validated_items = _validated_pac_fork_proof_items(items)
    validated_prune_policy = _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
    validated_site_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(site_policy)
    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
    if isinstance(moment, bool) or not isinstance(moment, int):
        raise TypeError("moment must be an int")
    if moment < 0:
        raise ValueError("moment must be non-negative")
    if not isinstance(issuer, str):
        raise TypeError("issuer must be a str")
    if issuer == "":
        raise ValueError("issuer must be non-empty")
    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
        raise TypeError("version must be an int")
    if version <= 0:
        raise ValueError("version must be positive")

    prune_policy_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _verdict_policy_bytes(validated_prune_policy)
    ).hexdigest()

    proof_digests = [
        hashlib.sha256(item[FORK_PROOF_ITEM_PROOF]).hexdigest()
        for item in validated_items
    ]
    rows = [
        _adjudicate_pac_fork_one(
            item, prune_policy_digest, validated_site_policy,
            validated_keyring, moment,
        )
        for item in validated_items
    ]

    contradicted, votes = _tally_pac_fork_rows(rows)

    edge_sets = set(votes.values())
    if contradicted or len(edge_sets) > 1:
        status = _PAFD_STATUS_CONFLICTED
        common = None
    elif len(edge_sets) == 1:
        common = _sorted_pac_fork_edge_objects(next(iter(edge_sets)))
        if len(votes) >= validated_site_policy[ADJ_THRESHOLD]:
            status = _PAFD_STATUS_ACCEPTED
        else:
            status = _PAFD_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT
    else:
        status = _PAFD_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT
        common = None

    rows.sort(
        key=lambda row: (
            row[VD_ISSUER] is not None,
            row[VD_ISSUER] or "",
            row[ID],
        )
    )

    signing_entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
        validated_keyring, issuer, version, moment
    )
    payload = {
        PAFD_COMMON: common,
        VD_ISSUER: issuer,
        ITEMS: [copy.deepcopy(row) for row in rows],
        KEY_VERSION: version,
        PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST: prune_policy_digest,
        PAFD_PROOFS: proof_digests,
        PAFD_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: hashlib.sha256(
            _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_site_policy)
        ).hexdigest(),
        STATUS: status,
        VERSION: PRUNE_AGGREGATE_FORK_DECISION_VERSION,
    }
    signature = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(signing_entry[SECRET]),
        _prune_compact(payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    return _prune_compact({TICKET_PAYLOAD: payload, SIGNATURE: signature})


def _parse_pafd(raw: object) -> tuple[dict, str]:
    """Validate decision bytes structurally into ``(payload, signature)``.

    A non-bytes argument or a field of the wrong type raises
    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int); every
    encoding, key-set, version, digest or value-format fault raises
    :class:`InvalidAggregateForkDecisionError`.  The policy, tally and
    credential bindings are checked by
    :func:`verify_prune_aggregate_fork_decision`.
    """
    if not isinstance(raw, bytes):
        raise TypeError("decision must be bytes")
    if not raw or raw[-1:] in (b"\n", b"\r", b" ", b"\t"):
        raise _pafd_invalid(
            "must end with the closing brace, no trailing byte"
        )
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise _pafd_invalid("is not valid UTF-8") from exc
    try:
        data = json.loads(
            text, object_pairs_hook=_reject_duplicate_pafd_keys
        )
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise _pafd_invalid("is not valid JSON") from exc

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise TypeError("decision must be a JSON object")
    if set(data.keys()) != _PAFD_DECISION_TOP_KEYS:
        raise _pafd_invalid(
            "must contain exactly the keys 'payload' and 'signature'"
        )
    signature = data[SIGNATURE]
    if not isinstance(signature, str):
        raise TypeError("decision signature must be a str")
    if not _prune_is_digest(signature):
        raise _pafd_invalid(
            "signature must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
        )
    payload = data[TICKET_PAYLOAD]
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise TypeError("decision payload must be an object")
    if set(payload.keys()) != _PAFD_PAYLOAD_KEYS:
        raise _pafd_invalid(
            "payload must contain exactly the keys 'common', 'issuer', "
            "'items', 'keyVersion', 'prunePolicyDigest', 'proofs', "
            "'sitePolicyDigest', 'status' and 'version'"
        )

    issuer = payload[VD_ISSUER]
    if not isinstance(issuer, str):
        raise TypeError("payload issuer must be a str")
    if issuer == "":
        raise _pafd_invalid("payload issuer must be a non-empty str")
    key_version = payload[KEY_VERSION]
    if isinstance(key_version, bool) or not isinstance(key_version, int):
        raise TypeError("payload keyVersion must be an int")
    if key_version <= 0:
        raise _pafd_invalid("payload keyVersion must be positive")
    status = payload[STATUS]
    if not isinstance(status, str):
        raise TypeError("payload status must be a str")
    if status not in _PAFD_STATUSES:
        raise _pafd_invalid("payload status is not a known status")
    for field in (PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST, PAFD_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST):
        digest = payload[field]
        if not isinstance(digest, str):
            raise TypeError(f"payload {field} must be a str")
        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
            raise _pafd_invalid(
                f"payload {field} must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
            )

    proofs = payload[PAFD_PROOFS]
    if not isinstance(proofs, list):
        raise TypeError("payload proofs must be a list")
    if not proofs:
        raise _pafd_invalid("payload proofs must be non-empty")
    for position, digest in enumerate(proofs):
        if not isinstance(digest, str):
            raise TypeError(f"payload proof {position} digest must be a str")
        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
            raise _pafd_invalid(
                f"payload proof {position} digest must be 64 lowercase hex "
                "characters"
            )

    raw_rows = payload[ITEMS]
    if not isinstance(raw_rows, list):
        raise TypeError("payload items must be a list")
    if not raw_rows:
        raise _pafd_invalid("payload items must be non-empty")
    parsed_rows: list[dict] = []
    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
    for position, row in enumerate(raw_rows):
        where = f"payload item {position}"
        if not isinstance(row, dict):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} must be an object")
        if set(row.keys()) != _PAFD_ROW_KEYS:
            raise _pafd_invalid(
                f"{where} must contain exactly the keys 'conclusion', "
                "'edges', 'id', 'keyVersion', 'proofDigest', 'reason' and "
                "'site'"
            )
        row_id = row[ID]
        if not isinstance(row_id, str):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} id must be a str")
        if row_id == "":
            raise _pafd_invalid(f"{where} id must be non-empty")
        if row_id in seen_ids:
            raise _pafd_invalid(f"{where} repeats an id")
        seen_ids.add(row_id)
        digest = row[PAFD_FORK_PROOF_DIGEST]
        if not isinstance(digest, str):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} proofDigest must be a str")
        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
            raise _pafd_invalid(
                f"{where} proofDigest must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
            )
        site = row[VD_ISSUER]
        if site is not None:
            if not isinstance(site, str):
                raise TypeError(f"{where} site must be a str or null")
            if site == "":
                raise _pafd_invalid(f"{where} site must be non-empty")
        row_key_version = row[KEY_VERSION]
        if isinstance(row_key_version, bool) or not isinstance(
            row_key_version, int
        ):
            if row_key_version is not None:
                raise TypeError(f"{where} keyVersion must be an int or null")
        elif row_key_version <= 0:
            raise _pafd_invalid(f"{where} keyVersion must be positive")
        if (site is None) != (row_key_version is None):
            raise _pafd_invalid(
                f"{where} site and keyVersion must be null together"
            )
        conclusion = row[ADJ_CONCLUSION]
        if not isinstance(conclusion, str):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} conclusion must be a str")
        if conclusion not in _PAFD_CONCLUSIONS:
            raise _pafd_invalid(f"{where} conclusion is not known")
        reason = row[ADJ_REASON]
        if conclusion == _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID:
            if reason is not None:
                raise _pafd_invalid(
                    f"{where} reason must be null for a valid item"
                )
        else:
            if not isinstance(reason, str):
                raise TypeError(f"{where} reason must be a str")
            if reason not in _PAFD_REASONS:
                raise _pafd_invalid(f"{where} reason is not known")
        if conclusion == _PAFD_CONCLUSION_INVALID:
            if reason not in _PAFD_INVALID_REASONS:
                raise _pafd_invalid(
                    f"{where} reason does not match an invalid item"
                )
        elif conclusion != _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID:
            if reason != conclusion:
                raise _pafd_invalid(
                    f"{where} reason must match its conclusion"
                )

        raw_edges = row[PAFD_EDGES]
        if raw_edges is not None:
            if not isinstance(raw_edges, list):
                raise TypeError(f"{where} edges must be a list or null")
            if not raw_edges:
                raise _pafd_invalid(
                    f"{where} edges must be non-empty for an authenticated "
                    "proof"
                )
            row_edges = [
                _validated_pafd_edge(value, where) for value in raw_edges
            ]
            triples = _pac_fork_edge_triples(row_edges)
            if len(set(triples)) != len(triples):
                raise _pafd_invalid(f"{where} edges must be unique")
            if list(triples) != sorted(triples):
                raise _pafd_invalid(f"{where} edges must be sorted ascending")
        identity_expected = reason != _PAFD_REASON_INVALID_PROOF
        if identity_expected:
            if site is None or raw_edges is None:
                raise _pafd_invalid(
                    f"{where} an authenticated proof must carry its site and "
                    "fork edges"
                )
        else:
            if site is not None or raw_edges is not None:
                raise _pafd_invalid(
                    f"{where} an invalid-proof item must carry no site or "
                    "fork edges"
                )
        parsed_rows.append(
            {
                ADJ_CONCLUSION: conclusion,
                PAFD_EDGES: (
                    None if raw_edges is None else [dict(edge)
                                                    for edge in row_edges]
                ),
                ID: row_id,
                KEY_VERSION: row_key_version,
                PAFD_FORK_PROOF_DIGEST: digest,
                ADJ_REASON: reason,
                VD_ISSUER: site,
            }
        )

    common = payload[PAFD_COMMON]
    if common is not None:
        if not isinstance(common, list):
            raise TypeError("payload common must be a list or null")
        if not common:
            raise _pafd_invalid(
                "a bound common edge set must be non-empty"
            )
        common_edges = [
            _validated_pafd_edge(value, "payload common")
            for value in common
        ]
        common_triples = _pac_fork_edge_triples(common_edges)
        if len(set(common_triples)) != len(common_triples) or list(
            common_triples
        ) != sorted(common_triples):
            raise _pafd_invalid(
                "payload common edges must be unique and sorted ascending"
            )

    decision_version = payload[VERSION]
    if isinstance(decision_version, bool) or not isinstance(
        decision_version, int
    ):
        raise TypeError("payload version must be an int")
    if decision_version != PRUNE_AGGREGATE_FORK_DECISION_VERSION:
        raise _pafd_invalid("payload version must be the integer 1")

    if _prune_compact(data) != raw:
        raise _pafd_invalid("encoding is not the canonical compact form")
    return payload, signature


def _reconcile_pafd(payload: dict, threshold: int) -> str:
    """Re-derive every aggregate binding of a parsed fork decision.

    Re-tallies the per-proof rows the signature covers -- row ordering,
    proof digests, duplicate/contradiction conclusions, the cross-site
    complete-edge-set agreement, the threshold acceptance and the
    claimed common set -- without seeing any fork proof.  Any mismatch
    raises :class:`InvalidAggregateForkDecisionError`; otherwise the
    derived status is returned.
    """
    rows = payload[ITEMS]
    proofs = payload[PAFD_PROOFS]
    if len(rows) != len(proofs):
        raise _pafd_invalid(
            "the items must cover every proof and vice versa"
        )
    expected_order = sorted(
        rows,
        key=lambda row: (
            row[VD_ISSUER] is not None,
            row[VD_ISSUER] or "",
            row[ID],
        ),
    )
    if [row[ID] for row in expected_order] != [row[ID] for row in rows]:
        raise _pafd_invalid("items must be sorted by site then id")
    row_digests = [row[PAFD_FORK_PROOF_DIGEST] for row in rows]
    if sorted(row_digests) != sorted(proofs):
        raise _pafd_invalid(
            "the bound proof digests must equal the per-item digests"
        )

    by_site: dict[str, dict[_PAFD_EDGE_SET, list[dict]]] = {}
    for row in rows:
        if row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] == _PAFD_CONCLUSION_INVALID:
            continue
        by_site.setdefault(row[VD_ISSUER], {}).setdefault(
            _pafd_content(row), []
        ).append(row)

    contradicted = False
    votes: dict[str, _PAFD_EDGE_SET] = {}
    for site, groups in by_site.items():
        if len(groups) > 1:
            contradicted = True
            expected_conclusion = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION
            expected_reason = REASON_CONTRADICTION
        else:
            expected_conclusion = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID
            expected_reason = None
            votes[site] = next(iter(groups.keys()))
        for members_raw in groups.values():
            members = sorted(members_raw, key=lambda row: row[ID])
            for index, row in enumerate(members):
                if index == 0:
                    if row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] != expected_conclusion:
                        raise _pafd_invalid(
                            f"item {row[ID]!r} has the wrong conclusion"
                        )
                    if row[ADJ_REASON] != expected_reason:
                        raise _pafd_invalid(
                            f"item {row[ID]!r} has the wrong reason"
                        )
                else:
                    if row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] != _PAFD_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE:
                        raise _pafd_invalid(
                            f"item {row[ID]!r} must be a duplicate"
                        )
                    if row[ADJ_REASON] != REASON_DUPLICATE:
                        raise _pafd_invalid(
                            f"item {row[ID]!r} must carry the duplicate "
                            "reason"
                        )
            representative = members[0]
            for row in members[1:]:
                if _pac_fork_edge_triples(
                    row[PAFD_EDGES]
                ) != _pac_fork_edge_triples(representative[PAFD_EDGES]):
                    raise _pafd_invalid(
                        f"item {row[ID]!r} duplicates a proof with a "
                        "different fork edge set"
                    )

    edge_sets = set(votes.values())
    if contradicted or len(edge_sets) > 1:
        status = _PAFD_STATUS_CONFLICTED
        expected_common = None
    elif len(edge_sets) == 1 and len(votes) >= threshold:
        status = _PAFD_STATUS_ACCEPTED
        expected_common = _sorted_pac_fork_edge_objects(
            next(iter(edge_sets))
        )
    elif len(edge_sets) == 1:
        status = _PAFD_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT
        expected_common = _sorted_pac_fork_edge_objects(
            next(iter(edge_sets))
        )
    else:
        status = _PAFD_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT
        expected_common = None

    if payload[STATUS] != status:
        raise _pafd_invalid("the status does not match the tallied items")
    if payload[PAFD_COMMON] != expected_common:
        raise _pafd_invalid(
            "the bound common edge set does not match the tallied items"
        )
    return status


def verify_prune_aggregate_fork_decision(
    decision, prune_policy, site_policy, keyring, moment
):
    """Re-verify a signed prune aggregate fork decision entirely offline.

    Only the decision bytes, the expected shared ``prune_policy``, the
    expected ``site_policy``, the current ``keyring`` and the
    verification ``moment`` are consulted -- no file is read or written
    and no argument is modified.  Verification validates the canonical
    encoding and every key set, recomputes both policy digests, re-tallies
    the bound per-proof rows purely from the signed payload (the
    original-order proof digest bindings, the site/id row ordering, the
    same-site duplicate/contradiction markings, the cross-site complete
    fork-edge-set agreement, the threshold outcome and the claimed
    common set), and checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the *current*
    keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version, usable at
    the verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry rejects
    the decision with no fallback.

    On success a fresh mapping is returned with the fixed keys
    ``common``, ``decisionDigest`` (the SHA-256 of the decision bytes),
    ``issuer``, ``items``, ``keyVersion``, ``prunePolicyDigest``,
    ``proofs``, ``sitePolicyDigest``, ``status`` and ``version`` (the
    integer 1).  A non-bytes decision or a public field of the wrong
    type raises :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an
    int); an illegal prune/site policy, keyring or moment raises
    :class:`ValueError`; an illegal encoding, key set, digest, ordering,
    tally or binding raises
    :class:`InvalidAggregateForkDecisionError` (a :class:`ValueError`
    subclass); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials
    or a signature mismatch raise :class:`AuthenticationError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(decision, bytes):
        raise TypeError("decision must be bytes")
    validated_prune_policy = _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
    validated_site_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(site_policy)
    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
    verify_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")
    return _verify_pafd_core(
        decision, validated_prune_policy, validated_site_policy,
        validated_keyring, verify_moment,
    )


def _verify_pafd_core(
    decision: bytes,
    validated_prune_policy: dict,
    validated_site_policy: dict,
    validated_keyring: dict[str, list[dict]],
    verify_moment: int,
) -> dict:
    """Verify one fork decision against already-validated shared materials.

    This is the shared core of
    :func:`verify_prune_aggregate_fork_decision` and the batch
    :func:`verify_prune_aggregate_fork_decisions`; the caller owns the
    argument-type and shared-material validation.  The returned dict is
    freshly built solely from authenticated decision material.
    """
    payload, signature = _parse_pafd(decision)
    expected_prune_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _verdict_policy_bytes(validated_prune_policy)
    ).hexdigest()
    if payload[PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST] != expected_prune_digest:
        raise _pafd_invalid("prune policy digest does not match the policy")
    expected_site_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_site_policy)
    ).hexdigest()
    if payload[PAFD_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST] != expected_site_digest:
        raise _pafd_invalid("site policy digest does not match the policy")

    status = _reconcile_pafd(
        payload, validated_site_policy[ADJ_THRESHOLD]
    )

    entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
        validated_keyring, payload[VD_ISSUER], payload[KEY_VERSION],
        verify_moment,
    )
    expected_signature = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(entry[SECRET]),
        _prune_compact(payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected_signature, signature):
        raise AuthenticationError(
            "prune aggregate fork decision signature does not match"
        )

    return {
        key: copy.deepcopy(value)
        for key, value in (
            (PAFD_COMMON, payload[PAFD_COMMON]),
            (FORK_PROOF_DIGEST, hashlib.sha256(decision).hexdigest()),
            (VD_ISSUER, payload[VD_ISSUER]),
            (ITEMS, payload[ITEMS]),
            (KEY_VERSION, payload[KEY_VERSION]),
            (PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST, expected_prune_digest),
            (PAFD_PROOFS, payload[PAFD_PROOFS]),
            (PAFD_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST, expected_site_digest),
            (STATUS, status),
            (VERSION, PRUNE_AGGREGATE_FORK_DECISION_VERSION),
        )
    }


# -- Offline batch verification of prune aggregate fork decisions -------------

PRUNE_AGGREGATE_FORK_DECISIONS_VERSION = 1

PFDA_DECISION = "decision"

_PFDA_DECISION_ITEM_KEYS = frozenset((ID, PFDA_DECISION))
_PFDA_DECISIONS_VERIFIED = _VERIFY_VERIFIED
_PFDA_DECISIONS_INVALID = _PRUNE_RECEIPT_VERIFY_INVALID
_PFDA_DECISIONS_UNAUTHENTICATED = VERIFY_UNAUTHENTICATED


def _validated_pfda_decision_items(items: object) -> list[dict]:
    """Validate the decision batch before any decision is parsed.

    The argument must be a non-empty list of dicts each holding exactly
    ``id`` (a non-empty str, unique across the batch) and ``decision``
    (bytes).  Container, element and field type faults raise
    :class:`TypeError`; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a
    wrong key set raises :class:`ValueError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        raise TypeError("items must be a list")
    if not items:
        raise ValueError("items must be a non-empty list")
    validated: list[dict] = []
    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
    for position, item in enumerate(items):

    item: dict,
    validated_prune_policy: dict,
    validated_site_policy: dict,
    validated_keyring: dict[str, list[dict]],
    moment: int,
) -> dict:
    """Verify one prune aggregate fork decision in isolation.

    Unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials and a wrong
    signature make the item ``unauthenticated``; every encoding,
    key-set, digest, ordering, tally or binding fault makes it
    ``invalid``; a passing decision is ``verified``.
    """
    item_id = item[ID]
    try:
        result = _verify_pafd_core(
            item[PFDA_DECISION],
            validated_prune_policy,
            validated_site_policy,
            validated_keyring,

            item_id, _PFDA_DECISIONS_UNAUTHENTICATED, str(exc), None

        # *inside* the decision bytes; the public argument types were
        # all validated before the batch ran.

            item_id, _PFDA_DECISIONS_INVALID, str(exc), None

PRUNE_AGGREGATE_CHAINS_VERSION = 1

PAC_BATCH_ROOT = "root"
PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS = "successors"
PAC_BATCH_POLICIES = "policies"

PAC_CHAINS_VERIFIED = "verified"
PAC_CHAINS_CONFLICTED = "conflicted"
PAC_CHAINS_INVALID_ROOT = "invalid-root"
PAC_CHAINS_INVALID_CHAIN = "invalid-chain"
PAC_CHAINS_UNAUTHENTICATED = "unauthenticated"

_PAC_CHAIN_ITEM_ERROR = "forked-aggregate-chain"

_PAC_CHAIN_ITEM_KEYS = frozenset((
    ID,
    PAC_BATCH_ROOT,
    PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS,
    PAC_BATCH_POLICIES,
))
_PAC_CHAIN_FORK_KEYS = frozenset((
    PAC_ROOT_DIGEST,
    PAC_PREDECESSOR_DIGEST,
    PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS,
    _FORK_IDS,
))


def _validated_pac_chain_batch(items: object) -> list[dict]:
    """Validate the prune aggregate chain batch before any chain runs.

    Each item holds exactly ``id`` (a non-empty str, unique across the
    batch), ``root`` (bytes), ``successors`` (a list of bytes, possibly
    empty) and ``policies`` (the complete versioned site policy
    history, one entry per stage).  Container, element and field type
    faults raise :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an
    int); an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong key set, an
    illegal policy, a wrong policy count or a root stage policy without
    ``policyVersion`` 1 raises :class:`ValueError`.  Only a fully
    validated batch comes back, as fresh item dicts with copied lists,
    so verification below never mutates the caller's objects.
    """
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        raise TypeError("items must be a list")
    if not items:
        raise ValueError("items must be a non-empty list")
    validated: list[dict] = []
    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
    for position, item in enumerate(items):
        where = f"item {position}"
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} must be a dict")
        if set(item.keys()) != _PAC_CHAIN_ITEM_KEYS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{where} must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'policies', "
                "'root' and 'successors'"
            )
        item_id = item[ID]
        if not isinstance(item_id, str):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} id must be a str")
        if item_id == "":
            raise ValueError(f"{where} id must be non-empty")
        if item_id in seen_ids:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate id {item_id!r}")
        seen_ids.add(item_id)
        root = item[PAC_BATCH_ROOT]
        if not isinstance(root, bytes):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} root must be bytes")
        successors = item[PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS]
        if not isinstance(successors, list):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} successors must be a list")
        for hop_index, successor in enumerate(successors):
            if not isinstance(successor, bytes):
                raise TypeError(f"{where} successor {hop_index} must be bytes")
        policies = item[PAC_BATCH_POLICIES]
        validated_policies = _pac_validated_policy_sequence(policies)
        if len(validated_policies) != len(successors) + 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{where} policies must provide one entry per chain stage "
                "(one more than the number of successors)"
            )
        if validated_policies[0][DS_POLICY_VERSION] != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{where} root stage policy must carry policyVersion 1"
            )
        validated.append({
            ID: item_id,
            PAC_BATCH_ROOT: root,
            PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS: list(successors),
            PAC_BATCH_POLICIES: list(policies),
        })
    return validated


def _pac_chain_edge_nodes(item: dict) -> list[str]:
    """The digest chain a batch item walks: root then each successor."""
    nodes = [hashlib.sha256(item[PAC_BATCH_ROOT]).hexdigest()]
    for successor in item[PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS]:
        nodes.append(hashlib.sha256(successor).hexdigest())
    return nodes


def _pac_chain_item_report(
    item_id: str, status: str, error: str | None, result: dict | None
) -> dict:
    """One prune aggregate chain batch report with the fixed key order."""
    return {
        CHECKPOINT_ITEM_ERROR: error,
        ID: item_id,
        VERDICT_ITEM_RESULT: result,
        STATUS: status,
    }


def _verify_pac_chain_item(
    item: dict, prune_policy: object, keyring: object, verify_moment: int
) -> dict:
    """Verify one batch chain in isolation and report its outcome.

    The root aggregate is verified on its own first, so a root fault is
    reported ``invalid-root`` while a successor or chain-binding fault
    is ``invalid-chain``; credential and signature faults are
    ``unauthenticated`` and a passing chain is ``verified``.  A
    :class:`TypeError` here can only come from a wrong field type
    *inside* a packet; the public argument types were all validated
    before the batch ran.
    """
    item_id = item[ID]
    root = item[PAC_BATCH_ROOT]
    successors = item[PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS]
    policies = item[PAC_BATCH_POLICIES]
    try:
        verify_prune_aggregate_chain(
            root, [], prune_policy, policies[:1], keyring, verify_moment
        )
    except AuthenticationError as exc:
        return _pac_chain_item_report(
            item_id, PAC_CHAINS_UNAUTHENTICATED, str(exc), None
        )
    except (InvalidPruneBatchAggregateError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        return _pac_chain_item_report(
            item_id, PAC_CHAINS_INVALID_ROOT, str(exc), None
        )
    try:
        result = verify_prune_aggregate_chain(
            root, successors, prune_policy, policies, keyring, verify_moment
        )
    except AuthenticationError as exc:
        return _pac_chain_item_report(
            item_id, PAC_CHAINS_UNAUTHENTICATED, str(exc), None
        )
    except (InvalidPruneBatchAggregateError, InvalidAggregateChainError,
            TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        return _pac_chain_item_report(
            item_id, PAC_CHAINS_INVALID_CHAIN, str(exc), None
        )
    return _pac_chain_item_report(
        item_id, PAC_CHAINS_VERIFIED, None, result
    )


def verify_prune_aggregate_chains(items, prune_policy, keyring, moment):
    """Verify a batch of prune aggregate chains and spot successor forks.

    Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty ``id``, its ``root``
    aggregate packet, its ordered ``successors`` packets and its
    per-stage ``policies`` history; ``prune_policy`` is the invariant
    original pruning policy shared by every chain, and ``keyring`` and
    ``moment`` keep their single-chain meaning.  The whole batch
    structure -- every key set, element type, policy count and the
    shared materials -- is validated before any chain is verified, so
    only these batch-level faults raise: container, element or field
    type faults raise :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses
    as an int) and an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong
    policy count or an illegal moment raises :class:`ValueError`.

    Each chain is then verified independently, in strict input order,
    through the exact :func:`verify_prune_aggregate_chain` rules: one
    chain's failure never stops a later chain or changes an earlier
    report.  A root fault reports ``invalid-root``, a successor or
    chain-binding fault ``invalid-chain`` and a credential or signature
    fault ``unauthenticated``, each with a null ``result``; a passing
    chain reports ``verified``.

    The verified chains are then grouped by their ``rootDigest`` and
    only successor trajectories under the same aggregate root are
    compared: the same predecessor digest pointing at two distinct
    successor digests is a fork (a mere prefix extension -- the same
    chain growing longer -- is not).  Every verified chain crossing a
    forking edge is reclassified ``conflicted`` with its verified
    result kept and its ``error`` fixed to ``"forked-aggregate-chain"``;
    invalid and unauthenticated chains are never reclassified.

    Returns a fresh dict with the fixed keys ``forks``, ``items`` and
    ``version`` (the integer 1).  ``forks`` is sorted by ``rootDigest``
    then ``predecessorDigest``; each entry carries exactly
    ``rootDigest``, ``predecessorDigest``, ``successors`` (the forking
    successor digests, ascending) and ``ids`` (the ascending ids of the
    chains crossing the edge).  Each item report preserves the input
    order and carries, in this key order, ``error`` (null exactly when
    verified), ``id``, ``result`` (the single-chain summary when the
    chain verified, otherwise null) and ``status``.  No file is read or
    written and no input is modified.
    """
    validated_items = _validated_pac_chain_batch(items)
    _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
    _validated_keyring(keyring)
    verify_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")

    reports: list[dict] = []
    results: list[dict | None] = []
    for item in validated_items:
        report = _verify_pac_chain_item(
            item, prune_policy, keyring, verify_moment
        )
        reports.append(report)
        results.append(report[VERDICT_ITEM_RESULT])

    # Fork detection within each aggregate-root group: one predecessor
    # digest pointing at two distinct successor digests, ignoring
    # chains that did not verify.
    groups: dict[str, dict[str, set[str]]] = {}
    for item, result in zip(validated_items, results):
        if result is None:
            continue
        nodes = _pac_chain_edge_nodes(item)
        edges = groups.setdefault(nodes[0], {})
        for upstream, downstream in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]):
            edges.setdefault(upstream, set()).add(downstream)
    fork_edges: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = {}
    for root_digest, edges in groups.items():
        for upstream, digests in edges.items():
            if len(digests) > 1:
                fork_edges[(root_digest, upstream)] = sorted(digests)
    edge_ids: dict[tuple[str, str], set[str]] = {
        edge: set() for edge in fork_edges
    }
    if fork_edges:
        for item, report, result in zip(validated_items, reports, results):
            if result is None:
                continue
            nodes = _pac_chain_edge_nodes(item)
            crosses_fork = False
            for upstream in nodes[:-1]:
                edge = (nodes[0], upstream)
                if edge in fork_edges:
                    edge_ids[edge].add(item[ID])
                    crosses_fork = True
            if crosses_fork:
                report[STATUS] = PAC_CHAINS_CONFLICTED
                report[CHECKPOINT_ITEM_ERROR] = _PAC_CHAIN_ITEM_ERROR

    forks = [
        {
            PAC_ROOT_DIGEST: root_digest,
            PAC_PREDECESSOR_DIGEST: predecessor,
            PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS: fork_edges[(root_digest, predecessor)],
            _FORK_IDS: sorted(edge_ids[(root_digest, predecessor)]),
        }
        for root_digest, predecessor in sorted(fork_edges)
    ]
    return {
        CHAINS_FORKS: forks,
        ITEMS: reports,
        VERSION: PRUNE_AGGREGATE_CHAINS_VERSION,
    }


# -- Signed fork proofs over a prune aggregate chain batch --------------------

PRUNE_AGGREGATE_FORK_PROOF_VERSION = 1

_PAC_FORK_PROOF_TOP_KEYS = frozenset((TICKET_PAYLOAD, SIGNATURE))

def _verify_fac_chain(
    root: bytes,
    successors: list,
    validated_prune_policy: dict,
    validated_site_policy: dict,
    validated_policies: list[dict],
    validated_keyring: dict[str, list[dict]],
    verify_moment: int,
) -> dict:
    """Verify one validated fork aggregate chain hop by hop."""
    root_result = _verify_pfda_core(
        root, validated_prune_policy, validated_site_policy,
        _pac_plain_site_policy(validated_policies[0]),
        validated_keyring, verify_moment,
    )
    root_digest = hashlib.sha256(root).hexdigest()
    view = _fac_root_view(root)
    head_packet = root
    head_status = root_result[STATUS]
    head_declaration = root_result[PFDA_DECLARATION]
    head_policy_version = validated_policies[0][DS_POLICY_VERSION]

    previous_packet = root
    for index, successor in enumerate(successors):
        hop = _verify_fac_hop(
            successor, view, hashlib.sha256(previous_packet).hexdigest(),
            validated_policies[index], validated_policies[index + 1],
            validated_prune_policy, validated_site_policy,
            validated_keyring, verify_moment,
        )
        view = hop["view"]
        previous_packet = successor
        head_packet = successor
        head_status = view[STATUS]
        head_declaration = view[PFDA_DECLARATION]
        head_policy_version = view[FAC_POLICY_VERSION]

    common_digest = None
    if head_declaration is not None:
        common_digest = hashlib.sha256(
            _prune_compact(head_declaration)
        ).hexdigest()
    return {
        FAC_ROOT_DIGEST: root_digest,
        FAC_HEAD_DIGEST: hashlib.sha256(head_packet).hexdigest(),
        FAC_HEIGHT: view[FAC_HEIGHT],
        FAC_POLICY_VERSION: head_policy_version,
        STATUS: head_status,
        FAC_COMMON_DIGEST: common_digest,
    }


def verify_fork_aggregate_chain(
    root, successors, prune_policy, site_policy, policies, keyring, moment
):
    """Verify one fork aggregate supersession chain hop by hop, offline.

    ``root`` is the chain's cross-site fork decision aggregate packet
    and ``successors`` the ordered successor packets (possibly empty
    for a height-zero chain).  ``prune_policy`` is the invariant
    original ``{"batch", "sites", "threshold"}`` pruning policy,
    ``site_policy`` the invariant fork-proof site policy and
    ``policies`` the complete versioned decision site policy history --
    one entry per stage (the root policy plus one per successor), so
    its length is ``len(successors) + 1`` and the first carries
    ``policyVersion`` 1.  Only the root, the ordered successors, the two
    invariant policies, the policy history, the current keyring and the
    verification moment are consulted; no file is read or written and
    no input is modified.

    An empty successor list still verifies the root in full.  For a
    non-empty chain every hop is re-checked: the root, predecessor and
    height links, the append-only decision prefix, the old/new policy
    digests and single-step version rule, the non-decreasing effective
    moment, the invariant prune and fork-proof site policies, the
    per-new-decision re-authentication and the full stage re-tally, the
    verdict state machine and dual-policy sealer authorization, and the
    exact-issuer/version HMAC with a credential usable at both the
    hop's effective moment and the verification moment.

    On success returns a fresh mapping with the fixed keys
    ``rootDigest``, ``headDigest``, ``height`` (0 for a bare root),
    ``policyVersion`` (the head policy's version), ``status`` and
    ``commonDigest`` (the SHA-256 of the canonical common declaration
    when one is bound, otherwise null); repeated calls return equal but
    mutually independent results.  A non-bytes argument or a public
    field of the wrong type raises :class:`TypeError`; an empty value,
    an illegal version, a wrong policy count or a backwards moment
    raises :class:`ValueError`; a bad root raises
    :class:`InvalidAggregateForkDecisionAggregateError`; a bad
    successor or chain binding raises
    :class:`InvalidForkAggregateChainError`; a credential or signature
    fault raises :class:`AuthenticationError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(root, bytes):
        raise TypeError("root must be bytes")
    if not isinstance(successors, list):
        raise TypeError("successors must be a list")
    for index, successor in enumerate(successors):
        if not isinstance(successor, bytes):
            raise TypeError(f"successor {index} must be bytes")
    validated_prune_policy = _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
    validated_site_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(site_policy)
    validated_policies = _pac_validated_policy_sequence(policies)
    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
    verify_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")
    if len(validated_policies) != len(successors) + 1:
        raise ValueError(
            "policies must provide one entry per chain stage (one more than "
            "the number of successors)"
        )
    if validated_policies[0][DS_POLICY_VERSION] != 1:
        raise ValueError("the root stage policy must carry policyVersion 1")

    return _verify_fac_chain(
        root, successors, validated_prune_policy, validated_site_policy,
        validated_policies, validated_keyring, verify_moment,
    )


# -- Offline batch verification and cross-chain fork detection -----------------

def _validated_fac_chain_batch(items: object) -> list[dict]:
    """Validate the fork aggregate chain batch before any chain runs.

    Each item holds exactly ``id`` (a non-empty str, unique across the
    batch), ``root`` (bytes), ``successors`` (a list of bytes, possibly
    empty) and ``policies`` (the complete versioned decision site
    policy history, one entry per stage).  Container, element and field
    type faults raise :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses
    as an int); an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong key
    set, an illegal policy, a wrong policy count or a root stage policy
    without ``policyVersion`` 1 raises :class:`ValueError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        raise TypeError("items must be a list")
    if not items:
        raise ValueError("items must be a non-empty list")
    validated: list[dict] = []
    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
    for position, item in enumerate(items):
        where = f"item {position}"
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} must be a dict")
        if set(item.keys()) != _FAC_CHAIN_ITEM_KEYS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{where} must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'policies', "
                "'root' and 'successors'"
            )
        item_id = item[ID]
        if not isinstance(item_id, str):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} id must be a str")
        if item_id == "":
            raise ValueError(f"{where} id must be non-empty")
        if item_id in seen_ids:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate id {item_id!r}")
        seen_ids.add(item_id)
        root = item[PAC_BATCH_ROOT]
        if not isinstance(root, bytes):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} root must be bytes")
        successors = item[PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS]
        if not isinstance(successors, list):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} successors must be a list")
        for hop_index, successor in enumerate(successors):
            if not isinstance(successor, bytes):
                raise TypeError(f"{where} successor {hop_index} must be bytes")
        policies = item[PAC_BATCH_POLICIES]
        validated_policies = _pac_validated_policy_sequence(policies)
        if len(validated_policies) != len(successors) + 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{where} policies must provide one entry per chain stage "
                "(one more than the number of successors)"
            )
        if validated_policies[0][DS_POLICY_VERSION] != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{where} root stage policy must carry policyVersion 1"
            )
        validated.append({
            ID: item_id,
            PAC_BATCH_ROOT: root,
            PAC_BATCH_SUCCESSORS: list(successors),
            PAC_BATCH_POLICIES: list(policies),
        })
    return validated


def _fac_chain_item_report(
    item_id: str, status: str, error: str | None, result: dict | None
) -> dict:
    """One fork aggregate chain batch report with the fixed key order."""
    return {
        CHECKPOINT_ITEM_ERROR: error,
        ID: item_id,
        VERDICT_ITEM_RESULT: result,
        STATUS: status,
    }


def _verify_fac_chain_item(
    item: dict, prune_policy: object, site_policy: object,
    keyring: object, verify_moment: int
) -> dict:
    """Verify one batch chain in isolation and report its outcome.

    The root aggregate is verified on its own first, so a root fault is

The proof is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object — recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing byte — carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`. The payload binds exactly `chains`, `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `policy` (the SHA-256 of the canonical compact prune policy), the complete `report` and `version` (integer 1); `chains` summarizes every input chain strictly in input order with none omitted, replaced or reordered, each entry binding exactly `id`, `root` (the SHA-256 of the root bytes), `successors` (the SHA-256 of each successor's bytes in chain order) and `policies` (the SHA-256 of each stage policy's canonical bytes in history order). The signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical payload under the exact issuer/version key; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.
176:`adjudicate_prune_aggregate_forks(items, prune_policy, site_policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` aggregates uniquely identified site fork proofs into one signed threshold decision, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id` and `proof` bytes. `prune_policy` is the shared invariant original `{"batch","sites","threshold"}` pruning policy the proofs were issued against and `site_policy` carries exactly `sites` (a non-empty map of each authorized non-empty site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and `threshold` (a positive integer no greater than the site count); `keyring`/`moment` keep their existing rules and `issuer`/`version` name the adjudicator credentials. Every proof is first verified through the existing prune aggregate fork proof rules (a future-dated or foreign-policy proof is an `invalid-proof` carrying no identity), then authorized precisely by the exact payload identity and key version against the site policy with no fallback (`unauthorized-site`, `unauthorized-version`), then authenticated against the current keyring (`credential-unavailable`, `revoked`, `not-yet-valid`, `expired`, `bad-signature`); an invalid, unauthenticated or unauthorized proof rejects only that item, keeping its fixed reason while later items are still processed. For one site the complete fork edge set — every edge of root digest, forking predecessor digest and the ascending set of legal successor digests — counts only once: an extra proof whose edge set is identical is `duplicate`, while two distinct complete edge sets from one site are a `contradiction`. Distinct sites must agree exactly on that complete edge set (root summaries, fork predecessors and legal successors together); any same-site contradiction or cross-site disagreement is `conflicted` with a null common set, never outvotable by a majority. A unique common edge set backed by at least the threshold of distinct sites is `accepted`; the same unique set short of the threshold is `insufficient` yet still binds that common set; with no valid vote at all the common set is null. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `common` (the stable-sorted common fork edge set, or null), `issuer`, `items` (the per-proof rows stably sorted by issuer then id, each carrying `conclusion`, the authenticated `edges` or null, `id`, `issuer`, `keyVersion`, the proof `digest` and `reason`), `keyVersion`, `prunePolicyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical prune policy), `proofs` (each input proof's SHA-256 in the original input order), `sitePolicyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical site policy — sites ascending, versions ascending), `status` and `version` (integer 1). The signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the exact issuer/version key. Parameter, container or public-field type faults raise `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, or an illegal prune/site policy, threshold, moment, issuer or version raises `ValueError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired adjudicator credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.
182:`verify_prune_aggregate_fork_decisions(items, prune_policy, site_policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a non-empty batch of signed prune aggregate fork decisions offline and in strict input order, in isolation. Each item contains exactly a non-empty, batch-unique `id` and the `decision` bytes `adjudicate_prune_aggregate_forks` produced; `prune_policy` is the shared invariant original pruning policy and `site_policy` the fork-proof site authorization policy the decisions were issued against. The whole batch structure and the shared policies, keyring and moment are validated in full before any decision is parsed, so a batch-level fault never yields a partial report (container/element/field type faults `TypeError`, a bool never posing as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key set `ValueError`, with the policies, keyring and moment keeping their single-decision classification).
